newsitem.title: USA: Tennant says Q1 results under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Tennant says Q1 results under pressure.

text.p: Tennant Co said Monday that first-quarter results were under pressure but it is optimistic about the outlook for the year.
"While our first quarter results are under pressure ... we expect to produce a stronger sales growth than in 1996," the company said.

"In addition, we are focused on improving our gross margins, which we believe will begin to show results by mid-year. This makes us reasonably confident that Tennant can report higher sales and earnings, and an improvement in operating margin, for 1997."

The maker of floor maintenance products said its expectations are based on "generally favorable economic forecasts for North America and most international markets, a recovery in our floor coatings business, and the considerable number of new and updated products already in our line or planned for 1997."

The company today reported 1996 net earnings of $21.0 million, up from $19.7 million in 1995. Net sales rose 6.0 percent to $344.4 million. It said a stronger dollar reduced sales by $3.3 million and cut net earnings by some $600,000.
Profit from operations for 1996 was $31.6 million, up 5.0 percent from 1995, resulting in an operating margin of 9.2 percent versus 9.3 percent for 1995.

"The change in operating margin was due to a 1.6-point decline in gross margin, which was partially offset by expense control measures that slowed the growth rate for selling and administrative expenses," the company said.
Tennant said its 6.0 percent annual sales gain was below the comparable growth achieved in the recent past.

"While the stronger dollar was a factor, the primary reasons were nearly flat orders for floor coatings products after several years of strong growth, and somewhat weaker than expected orders for industrial machines in North America.

"On the other hand, orders for commercial equipment products in general, and industrial equipment products in a number of key international markets, were up in the double-digit range," the company said.
